document_summary: Cleary Gottlieb law-firm alert (Jan. 6, 2026) on California's AB 325 and SB 763 amendments to the Cartwright Act, which restrict common pricing algorithms (statewide, not rental-specific).

rules.title: Cartwright Act amendments (AB 325): common pricing algorithm prohibition
rules.requirement: Businesses may not use or distribute common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade, and may not use or offer them while coercing users to adopt the algorithm's price or commercial-term recommendations. The alert names apartment rental companies as recent targets of algorithmic price-fixing claims.
rules.key_value: Ban on using or distributing common pricing algorithms to restrain trade, and on coercing adoption of their recommendations
rules.coverage_conditions: A pricing algorithm is 'common' if it has two or more users and uses competitor data to recommend or influence prices or other commercial terms. Applies to any industry, not only rental housing.
rules.exemptions: Single-firm or proprietary algorithms that use only the business's own data are not covered.
rules.interaction: Statewide antitrust law. The document does not address interaction with local rules such as San Francisco, Berkeley or other city algorithmic-rent ordinances.
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (as amended by A.B. 325)
rules.quoted_span: Businesses are expressly prohibited from using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source. It says Governor Newsom signed AB 325 and SB 763 'last October' (2025) and that they took effect January 1, 2026. The exact signing date is not stated, so adoption_date is null. The rule is a general antitrust provision, not rental-specific; it is recorded under algorithmic_rent_setting because it covers algorithmic price coordination affecting rents.
